name: input.capture
doc: Sneltoets instellen's key, captured by GNOME Shell (inputBridge.js: Main.pushModal, one key press, release; amendment 44): {accel} (a GTK accelerator name, through libxkbcommon), {disabled: true} (a plain Backspace: the shortcut is turned off) or {cancelled: true} (Esc, a click, the timeout or input.capture.cancel). Optional {timeout} in ms (1000-120000, default 30000); the bridge call waits 5 s longer. unsupported without the extension, or for a bridge that cannot wait yet (the grab is released then).

name: input.capture.cancel
doc: Ends a waiting input.capture (the bridge releases its grab and answers {cancelled: true}); {} also when nothing waits.

name: input.engineSetup
doc: The setup program of IBus engine {id}, started by GNOME Shell (launchBridge.js launch.ibusSetup: ibus-setup-<engine before ':'>.desktop with IBUS_ENGINE_NAME). bad_args for a malformed id, not_found when the engine has no setup, unsupported without the extension.

name: input.engines
doc: The IBus engines of /usr/share/ibus/component/*.xml that list their engines inline, without the xkb: ones: {engines: [{id, name, language, languageName, layout, setup}]} (setup: whether ibus-setup-<engine>.desktop is installed; a component that runs a program to list its engines is not run).

name: input.layouts
doc: The keyboard layouts and variants of xkeyboard-config's evdev.xml: {layouts: [{id, name, short, languages, countries}], languages: [{code, name}], countries: [{code, name}]}; id is layout or layout+variant, names in the UI language where xkeyboard-config's and iso-codes' catalogues have them.

name: input.options.set
doc: The special character keys in org.gnome.desktop.input-sources xkb-options: {lv3?, compose?}, each one of GNOME Settings' choices (lv3:lalt_switch ... lv3:ralt_alt for off; compose:ralt ... compose:ins) or null to remove that kind; an absent argument keeps it, every other option is kept. Answers {items, options}.

name: input.preview
doc: Shows keyboard layout {layout} (layout or layout+variant) in tecla, GNOME Settings' View Keyboard Layout. unsupported without tecla.

name: input.screenReader.preferences
doc: Verteller's Instellingen voor Verteller openen (amendment 36): ShowPreferences of the running Orca on the session bus (org.gnome.Orca.Service /org/gnome/Orca/Service, as GNOME Settings' Screen Reader Configure); Orca shows its own preferences window. {shown: true}; unsupported input.orcaNotRunning while no Orca owns the name (the screen reader is off), failed input.orcaFailed when Orca refuses or the call fails.

name: input.shortcuts
doc: GNOME Settings' keyboard shortcuts (its /usr/share/gnome-control-center/keybindings files, a built-in copy without them) and WinPoint's task-view and task-manager: {sections: [{id, title, items: [{schema, key, path, name, accels, default, isDefault, held, editable}]}], custom: [{id, path, name, command, binding}]}; held is {accel, setting} for the accelerator the extension holds from that key (amendment 13); title and name are GNOME's English texts, the page shows its own.

name: input.shortcuts.custom.add
doc: A custom shortcut {name, command, binding, replace?} at the first free custom<N> of media-keys custom-keybindings: {id, path}, or {conflict: {schema, key, path, id, name, accel}} and nothing written while another shortcut has the binding and replace is not true.

name: input.shortcuts.custom.remove
doc: Removes custom shortcut {id} from custom-keybindings and resets its keys, as GNOME Settings does.

name: input.shortcuts.custom.update
doc: Changes custom shortcut {id} (name?, command?, binding?, replace?); a binding another shortcut has is a {conflict} as for custom.add.

name: input.shortcuts.reset
doc: Resets one catalogued shortcut {schema, key} (g_settings_reset).

name: input.shortcuts.resetAll
doc: Resets every GNOME shortcut of the catalogue that is installed and writable; WinPoint's two and the custom shortcuts are kept, as GNOME Settings keeps its custom ones. Answers {reset: n}.

name: input.shortcuts.set
doc: Sets catalogued shortcut {schema, key, accels} (at most four GTK accelerators; [] turns it off). An accelerator another shortcut has (also WinPoint's held ones) answers {conflict: {schema, key, path, id, name, accel}} and writes nothing, unless replace is true: then it is taken from the other shortcut first ({items, replaced}).

name: input.sources.activate
doc: Switches the session to input source {index} (0-63) as GNOME's keyboard menu does, through the extension (inputBridge.js, GNOME Shell's InputSourceManager); for the tray's input indicator (amendment 15). not_found for a source that is not set up, unsupported without the extension.

name: input.sources.current
doc: The session's input sources as GNOME Shell's InputSourceManager has them: {sources: [{index, type, id, name, short}], current}, through the extension; events input.sourceChanged {current, id, short} and input.sourcesChanged. For the tray's input indicator (amendment 15). unsupported without the extension.

name: input.sources.set
doc: Writes org.gnome.desktop.input-sources sources {sources: [[type, id]]} (xkb layout[+variant] or an IBus engine; duplicates dropped). Then, as Ubuntu's GNOME Settings, the system keyboard: pkexec /usr/libexec/gnome-control-center-set-debian-keyboard <layouts> <variants> [options] in the background, only when polkit allows org.gnome.controlcenter.set-keyboard without asking; systemKeyboard is checking or skipped, and the event input.changed {what: systemKeyboard, ok} follows the helper.

name: input.tablet.mapButtons
doc: GNOME Shell's pad OSD in edition mode for {vidpid} (a tablet whose pad has buttons, rings, strips or dials), through the extension (inputBridge.js input.padOsd); the OSD writes the pad-button keys itself. bad_args for a malformed id, not_found for an absent tablet, unsupported without a pad or without the extension.

name: input.tablets
doc: The drawing tablets and pen displays (udev, /sys and libwacom: {vidpid, name, kind tablet|display|builtin, pen, pad, buttons, rings, strips, dials, reversible, styli}; styli holds default-<vidpid>, the stylus id of pens without a serial, the page adds GTK's serials), the touchscreens ({vidpid, name}, amendment 8) and the monitors for the output key (DisplayConfig: {connector, vendor, product, serial, name, builtin}).
